title: Intercom's Ad Strategy: It Doesn't Advertise Intercom, It Advertises Fin
summary: Intercom runs 1,550 Meta ads for Fin, not Intercom: 25 distinct creatives, a 3-day median ad life, 301 account-based ads and 821 sharing one headline.
body_markdown:
Intercom is the most-purchased AI Support Bots vendor in Ramp's October 2026 AI category data. 46% of buyers in the category chose it.


And Intercom does not advertise Intercom. On Meta it advertises Fin, on fin.ai. 1,550 ads since October 2025, and only 77 of them land on intercom.com.


1,550 ads is a lot. Underneath it sit 25 distinct creatives. The rest is the same ad, copied.


## Intercom ads: key findings


- **1,550** Meta ads since October 2025, **243** live as of 13 October 2026, all on Facebook and Instagram
- **25** distinct creatives behind them. The two biggest account for **778** ads, 50% of the total
- **821** ads (53%) share one headline: "See why Fin is the #1 AI Agent"
- **87%** of ads land on fin.ai. Only **77** go to intercom.com
- Median ended ad ran **3 days** . 57% of ended ads ran 3 days or less
- **301** ads point to five account-based landing pages ending in "-abm"
- **497** LinkedIn ads are bought through Influ2, person-level ads, in **10** campaigns, one per landing page, split across **47** audience IDs
- Those LinkedIn ads target hand-built lists of 15 to 48 towns: Kortrijk, Tolochenaz, Balsam Lake, Fröndenberg
- The offers run in sales order: a report from May, a Gartner renewals page from July, a Salesforce page with **77** new ads in October alone
- Startups get the first year free off a **$903** -a-month list price, but only with a partner's referral
- **126** ads replay the Pioneer 2025 event. **77** push an ROI calculator
- Google has **1,795** search ads across 46 regions, **82%** to intercom.com. LinkedIn has **825** ads, and every one with a destination goes to fin.ai


## How Intercom's funnel is wired


Intercom's feed ads aren't aimed at an audience. They're aimed at a list.


### LinkedIn runs through a person-level tool


Every LinkedIn ad with a destination, 497 of them, carries utm_source=Influ2. Influ2 sells ads aimed at named people inside named accounts. The campaign tag is an ID, not a name, and there are 10 of them, one per landing page:


Landing page Influ2 campaigns LinkedIn ads


fin.ai/built/for-support 4 202


/drlp/2026-customer-transformation-report-abm 1 88


fin.ai/roi-calculator 1 74


/drlp/integrations-salesforce-abm 1 63


/drlp/gartner-ai-agent-renewals-abm 1 48


/drlp/cx-quality-guide-abm 1 8


pioneer.fin.ai 1 14


Under the campaigns sit 47 audience IDs in the utm_term, +563903, +455921, +441464. Each is a slice of the target list.


### The targeting reads like a CRM export


497 LinkedIn ads target a list of 15 to 48 places. Not countries. Towns. New York and Dallas, then Kortrijk in Belgium, Tolochenaz in Switzerland, Balsam Lake in Wisconsin, Fröndenberg and Ahlen in Germany, Truckee in California.


Nobody picks Balsam Lake as a market. Those are where the target accounts sit. The location list is the account list, reverse-engineered into geography.


### The URL tells the page what to do


821 Meta ads link to fin.ai/built/for-support?demo. 297 Meta ads and 207 LinkedIn ads link to the account-based pages with ?dl=true. One flag opens the demo request, the other hands over the download. The ad decides which conversion the page asks for.


### The offers run in the order of a sales cycle


Offer When the Meta ads went out Who it's for


Pioneer 2025 replay Nov 2025 to Feb 2026, 126 ads Anyone curious


2026 customer transformation report May to Aug 2026, 77 in June A buyer forming a view


Gartner "AI Agent ROI Reality Check" July and August, then again in October Someone who bought an AI agent and faces a renewal


Fin inside Salesforce 3 ads in August, 13 in September, 77 in October Teams on Service Cloud, the home of Agentforce


The Salesforce page is the one rising now. It meets Service Cloud teams where they already work, while Salesforce sells them its own agent.


**Make the location list your account list.** When a platform won't take an account upload, the towns where your targets sit are the next best thing.


## How Intercom pays partners


Intercom doesn't run creator ads, and no affiliate program for individuals turned up. Its creator work stays off the ad account: a vendor case study credits a campaign with 12 to 14 AI and customer-service creators for its transformation report, run as their own posts. The rest of its incentives go through partners.


Program What it pays


Startup Partner Program Year one free off a $903-a-month list price, 50% off year two, 25% off year three. Seed to Series A, under 25 people, and a referral from a partner (a VC, an accelerator, a bank) is required


Solution Partner Program Agencies and consultancies earn a commission on clients they refer. The rate isn't public


The startup deal has a catch in the small print. Fin isn't discounted. A startup gets 315 free Fin outcomes a month in year one, 165 in year two, 90 in year three, and pays list price past that.


The seat is free. The AI agent is metered. Every VC and accelerator in the partner network hands Intercom a future Fin customer for the price of a year of seats.


## Part 1: The brand it does not advertise


### Every ad is a Fin ad


The Meta page is called Intercom. The ads are for Fin, Intercom's AI agent, and the product has its own domain.


Where the ad lands Ads Share


fin.ai 1,347 87%


pioneer.fin.ai (event replay) 126 8%


intercom.com (pricing ROI calculator) 77 5%


I counted twelve different headlines across 1,550 ads. Every one of them is about Fin, or about an AI agent. The company that got famous for the chat bubble has stopped asking for clicks on it.


The 46% Ramp number explains why that works. In Ramp's October 2026 AI category data, Intercom is the most-purchased vendor among AI Support Bots buyers. When the brand already wins the category, the ad budget goes to the product that is growing.


### 25 creatives, 1,550 ads


Meta groups ads that share one creative into a single family. Intercom has 25 families. The median family holds 27 ads. The biggest holds 465.


Biggest creative families Ads Share of 1,550


Family 1 465 30%


Family 2 313 20%


Family 3 144 9%


Family 4 (Pioneer replay) 126 8%


Family 5 93 6%


Other 20 families 409 26%


Five families are 74% of everything Intercom has launched. Volume of ad objects, not volume of creative.


### The 821


One line does most of the work. "See why Fin is the #1 AI Agent", over the body copy "Fin is the best-performing AI Agent for customer service, powerful enough to resolve even the most complex queries like refunds, account changes, technical troubleshooting, and more." 821 ads. All of them go to fin.ai/built/for-support, the main support page.


That is three creatives, run 821 times. A new ad object here is not a new idea. It is the same idea in a new audience, placement or budget bucket.


## Part 2: The ads churn, the creative does not


### Three days


1,429 of the 1,550 ads have ended. The median one ran 3 days. 820 ran 3 days or less.


The creative under those ads lives a median 110 days. The ad object lives 3.


Short, and I think it is deliberate. When the ad object turns over every few days and the creative underneath stays put, you are watching a testing machine that rotates audiences or budgets through a fixed set of messages. The winner is not killed. Its container is.


Month New ads


June 2026 383


July 2026 237


August 2026 176


September 2026 97


October 2026 (to the 13th) 169


June was the peak at 383. 201 ads launched in the last 30 days. 243 are live now.


### Video leads, and the biggest claim is all video


947 video ads, 603 image ads. The #1 claim is all video: 821 of 821. It plays clean: a wordmark, a sentence, a line of small text. No stock, no faces.


"The AI your support team needs, right inside Salesforce." 93 ads, run on Meta and LinkedIn. 13 October 2026.


## Part 3: Account-based marketing, on Meta


Five landing paths contain "drlp" and end in "-abm". That is the naming of a landing page built for a named list of accounts, not for the open feed.


Account-based lander Meta ads Asset behind it


/drlp/2026-customer-transformation-report-abm 144 Customer transformation report


/drlp/integrations-salesforce-abm 93 Fin inside Salesforce Service Cloud


/drlp/gartner-ai-agent-renewals-abm 33 Gartner survey on AI agent renewals


/drlp/cx-quality-guide-abm 24 CX quality guide


/drlp/demo-insights-abm 7 Demo and insights


301 ads. 19% of the account. I cannot see who they are aimed at, but the paths say what Intercom is doing: running enterprise account-based campaigns inside a feed most people use for photos.


The 2026 Customer Service Transformation Report. 144 ads, all to one account-based lander. 13 October 2026.


The offer changes by buyer stage. A report for the reader who is still forming a view. A Salesforce integration page for the team already on Service Cloud. A Gartner renewals page for the person who bought an AI agent and is worried about the renewal. Same product, three different doors.


### Same assets on LinkedIn


The same assets run on LinkedIn, at about half the Meta volume. 825 ads: 606 single-image, 214 video, 3 job ads and 2 follow-company ads. 199 say "See why Fin is the #1 AI Agent". 123 offer the report, 120 push "See your savings in seconds with Fin" (the ROI calculator), 117 say "Fin outperforms every time", 113 say "The AI your support team needs" and 93 run the Gartner "AI Agent ROI Reality Check".


LinkedIn ads with a destination Ads


fin.ai/built/for-support 202


Account-based landers ("-abm"): report 88, Salesforce 63, Gartner 48, CX guide 8 207


fin.ai/roi-calculator 74


pioneer.fin.ai 14


intercom.com 0


497 LinkedIn ads show a destination. 483 go to fin.ai, 14 to the Pioneer site and none to intercom.com. 207 of them, 42%, go to the account-based pages, a much higher share than on Meta's 19%. Same message, aimed more at named accounts.


## Part 4: Verticals, an event and a calculator


### Vertical landers


Lander Ads


fin.ai/solutions/financial-services 34


fin.ai/built/for-ecommerce 30


fin.ai/built/for-fintech 13


The copy is written for the vertical, not swapped in. The financial services ad promises accurate resolution of "card issues and transaction disputes". The ecommerce ad names "missing items and fraudulent orders". 77 ads, small next to the 821, and each one narrower.


The ecommerce version: a refund conversation shown in the Fin chat window. 13 October 2026.


### Pioneer 2025, replayed


126 ads, one video family, one lander on its own subdomain. The copy: "Catch up on all the major announcements from Pioneer 2025 - like the launch of Fin 3 - plus our vision for the future of AI customer experience."


The event was last year and Intercom is still paying to show the replay. It is cheaper than making new creative, and the event already did the persuading.


### An ROI calculator


77 ads push "Try our ROI calculator" to intercom.com/pricing/fin-roi, the one place the ad stream touches the Intercom domain. A further 4 go to fin.ai/roi-calculator. The ad itself shows a calculator, with the output on screen.


The ROI calculator ad. 77 ads to one pricing-page calculator. 13 October 2026.


## Part 5: Google still sells Intercom


Search is where the brand name comes back. Intercom has 1,795 Google text ads across 46 regions, the oldest first shown in March 2023. 1,475 of them (82%) land on intercom.com. 319 (18%) land on fin.ai.


Google headline Ads


Intercom: A Better Alternative 125


Fin. The #1 AI Agent 102


Ready to Upgrade? Try Intercom 94


Intercom Fin: AI Support Agent 45


Live Chat for Websites 31


Look at the first and third rows. "A Better Alternative" and "Ready to Upgrade? Try Intercom" are written for someone searching a competitor's name. One description reads "Intercom has everything they have, plus everything they don't." That is conquesting, and it sells the Intercom name.


The split is the point. On Meta, 5% of ads land on intercom.com. On LinkedIn, 0%. On Google, 82%. Someone typing a query already knows to look for Intercom. Someone scrolling Instagram or LinkedIn has to be introduced to Fin.


## What actually makes this work


The product has a name and a domain of its own, so the ad never has to explain the company. Fin is the thing in every frame.


The creative budget goes to 25 ideas, each run at scale. The three-day ad life is a test rig on top of them. If you only count ads, Intercom looks like an account that launches a hundred things a week. If you count creatives, it is a small, disciplined set.


And the landers do the segmenting. A report for the browser, Salesforce for the integrator, Gartner for the skeptic, a calculator for the person with a spreadsheet open. Nothing on the ad changes the claim. The page does.
